name: opening_drive_reversal_001_5s
author: adapted from cursor-fast
thesis: This strategy exploits opening-drive exhaustion after the first burst of post-auction directional flow in liquid NSE names. The inefficiency exists because market orders, stop runs, and emotional retail participation exaggerate the initial impulse, and it persists because fading the open is operationally hard, path-dependent, and vulnerable to real information gaps.
mechanism: Order flow imbalance between aggressive buyers and sellers creates short-term price pressure. When buy-side aggression exceeds sell-side by a threshold, the order book tilts and market makers adjust their quotes upward. This creates a 15-45 second drift before the book rebalances as new limit orders arrive to capture the improved price.

exit.signal_exit: exit when close touches vwap OR opening impulse resumes through signal bar extreme

weaknesses: Performance is regime-dependent and weakens materially when session structure changes mid-trade.
Fast moves can create worse-than-assumed slippage and reduce realized edge versus paper assumptions.
Crowding risk can compress payoff and make execution quality unstable in the most obvious setups.
prior_art: Opening drive fade with VWAP and wick confirmation
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
